questions.q: The coefficient of $x^n$ in the expansion of $\frac{e^{7 x}+e^x}{e^{3 x}}$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\frac{e^{7 x}+e^x}{e^{3 x}} \Rightarrow e^{4 x}+e^{-2 x}$
Series of $e^a=1+\frac{a}{1!}+\frac{a^2}{2!}+\frac{a^3}{3!} \ldots\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow e^{4 x}+ & e^{-2 x}=\left(1+\frac{4 x}{1!}+\frac{(4 x)^2}{2!}+\frac{(4 x)^3}{3!}+\ldots\right) \\
& +\left(1+\frac{(-2 x)}{1!}+\frac{(-2 x)^2}{2!}+\ldots \ldots\right)
\end{aligned}$
Here, coefficient of
$\begin{aligned}
& x^2 \equiv \frac{4^2}{2!}+\frac{(-2)^2}{2!} \\
& x^3 \equiv \frac{4^3}{3!}+\frac{(-2)^3}{3!} \\
& \vdots \\
& x^n=\frac{4^n}{n!}+\frac{(-2)^n}{n!}
\end{aligned}$

The coefficient of the highest power of $x$ in the expansion of 
$\left(x+\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)^8+\left(x-\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)^8$
questions.solution:
Since $\left(x+\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)^8+\left(x-\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)^8\begin{array}{r}=2\left\{{ }^8 C_0 x^8+{ }^8 C_2 x^6\left(x^2-1\right)+{ }^8 C_4 x^4\left(x^2-1\right)^2\right. \\ \left.+{ }^8 C_6 x^2\left(x^2-1\right)^3+{ }^8 C_8 x^0\left(x^2-1\right)^4\right\}\end{array}
So coefficient of highest power of $x=2$\left$\{{ }^8 C_0+{ }^8 C_2+{ }^8 C_4+{ }^8 C_6+{ }^8 C_8\right\}=(1+1)^8+(1-1)^8=2^8=256

questions.q: If $x^{18}$ occurs in the rth term in the expansion of $\left(x^4+\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{15}$, then what is the value of $r$ ?
questions.solution:
In the expansion of $\left(x^4+\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{15}$, let $T_r$ is the $r^{\text{th }}$ term
$\begin{aligned} \\ T_r & =\binom{15}{r-1}\left(x^4\right)^{15-r+1}\left(\frac{1}{x^3}\right)^{r-1} \\ \\ & =\binom{15}{r-1} x^{64-4 r-3 r+3}=15_{C_{r-1}} x^{67-7 r} \\ \end{aligned}$
$\mathrmx^{18}$ occurs in this term
$\Rightarrow 18=67-7 r \Rightarrow 7 r=49 \Rightarrow r=7 .$

questions.q: The coefficient of the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(\sqrt{\frac{x}{3}}+\frac{3}{2 x^{2}}\right)^{10}$ is
questions.solution:
The $(r+1)$ th term in the expansion of $\left(\sqrt{\frac{x}{3}}+\frac{3}{2 x^{2}}\right)^{10}$ is given by

$\begin{array}{l}

\mathrm{T}_{r+1}={ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_{r}\left(\sqrt{\frac{x}{3}}\right)^{10-r}\left(\frac{3}{2 x^{2}}\right)^{r} \\

={ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_{r} \frac{x^{5-\left(\frac{r}{2}\right)}}{3^{5-\left(\frac{r}{2}\right)}} \cdot \frac{3^{r}}{2^{r} x^{2 r}} \\

={ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_{r} \frac{3^{\left(\frac{3 r}{2}\right)-5}-5-\left(\frac{5 r}{2}\right)}{2^{r}} x

\end{array}

\mathrm{T}_{r+1}={ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_{r}\left(\sqrt{\frac{x}{3}}\right)^{10-r}\left(\frac{3}{2 x^{2}}\right)^{r}={ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_{r} \frac{x^{5-\left(\frac{r}{2}\right)}}{3} \cdot \frac{3^{r}}{2^{r} x^{2 r}}={ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_{r} \frac{3^{\left(\frac{3 r}{2}\right)-5}-\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{5 r}{2}\right)}{2^{r}}$x$ For  \mathrm{T}_{r+1} to be independent of $x$, we must have $5-$\left(\frac{5 r}{2}\right)=$0$ or $r=2$.

Thus, the 3 rd term is independent of $x$ and is equal to ${ }^{10} $\mathrm{C}_{2} \frac{3^{3-5}}{2^{2}}=\frac{10 \times 9}{2} \times \frac{3^{-2}}{4}=\frac{5}{4}$

$\left(1 + x\right)n\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)n = C0 n \left(2 + x\right)n \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + C1 n \left(2 + x\right)n - 1 \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)1 + \ldots + Cn n \cdot \dfrac{1}{xn}$

$∴$ Coefficient of $x^{- n} = Cn n = 1$

& \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}-12=-3 \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=9
\end{aligned}$$\)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: With 17 consonants and 5 vowels the number of words of four letters that can be formed having two different vowels in the middle and one consonant, repeated or different at each end is
questions.solution:
The two letters, the first and the last of the four lettered word can be chosen in \((17)^2\) ways, as repetition is allowed for consonants. The two vowels in the middle are distinct so that the number of ways of filling up the two places is \({ }^5 $\mathrm{P}_{2}=$20\).
The no. of different words \(=(17)^2 \cdot20=5780\).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The general solution of \(8 \tan ^2 $\frac{x}{2}=$1+\sec x\) is
questions.solution:
We have, \(8 \tan ^2 $\frac{x}{2}=$1+\sec x\)
$\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow 8 $\left(\frac{1-\cos x}{1+\cos x}\right)=$1+$\frac{1}{\cos x}=\frac{1+\cos x}{\cos x}$\\
& \Rightarrow 8 \cos x-8 \cos ^2 x=(1+\cos x)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow 9 \cos ^2 $\mathrm{x}-$6 \cos $\mathrm{x}+$1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(3 \cos $\mathrm{x}-$1)^2=0 \Rightarrow 3 \cos $\mathrm{x}-$1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \cos $\mathrm{x}=\frac{1}{3}=\cos \alpha \text{ (say) }  \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=$2 $\mathrm{n} \pi \pm \alpha$\\
& \therefore $\mathrm{x}=$2 $\mathrm{n} \pi \pm \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \text{ where } \mathrm{n} \in \mathrm{I}
\end{aligned}$
